editorial.headline: Timepiece Retail: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This retail activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s island-wide risk moratorium blocks it for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
In Bali, a foreigner cannot register this retail activity as PMA today, even though its national position is open. KBLI 47734 covers the retail sale of varied timepieces: wristwatches, pocket watches, wall clocks, alarm clocks and bells. It also covers retail sales of watch and clock parts. The scope places the activity outside direct sales, keeping the description anchored in the retailing of timekeeping goods and their components. Its stated range runs from personal watches to wall clocks, alarms, bells and their retail parts.

That business is open to registration at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. At the national level, the PMA status is Open and the permitted foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. A PMA company therefore has a national route to full foreign ownership of this activity; the record does not present a partial foreign-share limit. The cited national basis is Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021. For founders assessing the activity outside the Bali restriction, the availability of all four listed scales and the 100% ceiling are the essential national facts.

Bali, however, answers a different question: whether the activity may be registered there as PMA. The answer is no. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the reason identifies the OSS risk at the Large scale as Low/Medium-Low across every scope. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration. It is an island-wide, permanent rule. The result is a complete block on PMA registration in Bali, rather than a reduced foreign-ownership percentage.

This is why the national and Bali positions should not be blended. Nationally, the record permits up to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, the moratorium prevents PMA registration of the same activity. The difference is not a question of the product range: wristwatches, clocks, alarms, bells and parts remain the defined retail scope. It is a location-specific PMA outcome arising from the stated risk classification and Bali rule. For this code, a full national foreign-ownership ceiling does not produce a Bali PMA registration route.
